newsitem.title: GERMANY: Strauss-Kahn again says Paris may hit EMU goal.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn again says Paris may hit EMU goal.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn reaffirmed his belief that Paris may undershoot budget deficit targets needed to qualify for monetary union in a German newspaper interview on Wednesday.

Strauss-Kahn told the Handelsblatt daily that France would come very near or even slip under the three percent deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) target stipulated by the Maastricht Treaty for countries joining monetary union.
Handelsblatt distributed a summary of the article on Wednesday ahead of full publication of its article on Thursday.
Strauss-Kahn made nearly the same remarks to another German newspaper, Die Zeit, in an interview which Die Zeit distributed to the media earlier on Wednesday.
He was quoted by Handelsblatt as saying he believed "that we will come very near to three percent and with a bit of luck may even come in under".
"I am hopeful that economic growth will accelerate by the end of the year and that tax income will come in stronger than expected," Handelsblatt quoted Strauss-Kahn as saying.
He also said that barring a disaster like a worldwide economic crisis, France would surely have a budget deficit no larger than 3.3 percent of GDP.

Strauss-Khan told the paper that countries hoping to qualify for monetary union should not be too preoccupied with meeting the budget criteria alone and that all the economic targets stipulated by Maastrict should be taken into account when deciding who qualifies for the single currency project.
"Germany is sticking to a budget deficit of 3.0 percent," he said. "But one should not concentrate only on a single one of the five Maastricht criteria," he said.
